summary.short: Amends federal criminal statutes in title 18 (mail, wire and bank fraud, money laundering, and impersonation of federal officials) to set higher fines and prison terms where the offence is committed with AI assistance. Introduced bill, pending.
summary.long: The AI Fraud Deterrence Act amends federal criminal law in title 18 of the United States Code. Its findings (Sec. 2) cite 2025 incidents in which AI was used to impersonate senior US officials. Mail fraud (Sec. 3(a)) and wire fraud (Sec. 3(b)): the general fine rises from $1,000,000 to $2,000,000, and an AI-assisted violation is subject to a fine of not more than $1,000,000 or imprisonment of not more than 20 years, or both. Bank fraud (Sec. 3(c)) gets a new subsection (b): AI-assisted violations carry a fine of not more than $2,000,000 or imprisonment of not more than 30 years, or both. Money laundering (Sec. 3(e)) carries, for AI-assisted violations, a fine of not more than $1,000,000 or thrice the value involved, whichever is greater, or imprisonment of not more than 20 years. Sec. 3(d) and 3(e)(2) define 'artificial intelligence' by reference to section 5002 of the National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020. Impersonation of federal officials (Sec. 4, amending 18 U.S.C. 912) adds an AI-assisted penalty of not more than $1,000,000 or 3 years, and a rule of construction that does not limit AI use in satire or parody if the content clearly discloses that it is not authentic. The bill states no effective date.

relations.note: Amended by Secs. 3(a)-(e) and 4(1)-(4). Adds AI-assisted penalty clauses, an AI definition in §§ 1346(2) and 1956(c)(10), and a rule of construction and definition in § 912(b)-(c). Target is the code, not a registry instrument.

notes: Introduced bill text; no version date appears in the document. Possible internal inconsistency: Sec. 3(a)(1) and 3(b)(1) raise the base fine under 18 U.S.C. 1341 and 1343 from $1,000,000 to $2,000,000, while the AI-assisted clauses added by Sec. 3(a)(2) and 3(b)(2) set a fine of $1,000,000 for the same offences, which is lower than the base fine. Sec. 3(c)(2) (§ 1344(b)) sets $2,000,000 and 30 years. Sec. 4(1) sets $1,000,000 and 3 years for § 912. Sec. 4(4), subsection (b), lacks a closing quotation mark. Sec. 2 findings describe 2025 incidents and are not operative provisions.

events.note: The fetched bill text contains no dated events. It has no effective-date, application, phase-in, deadline, sunset or repeal provision, and no introduction date or legislative history. The only dates in the text are the dates of the events it describes in its findings (May 2025 and July 2025), which are not events of this instrument.

thresholds.note: No numeric cutoff that changes scope, eligibility, exemption, obligation tier, prohibition or benefit was found. The numbers in Sec. 3 and Sec. 4 are penalty maxima (fine amounts, imprisonment terms, and the thrice-the-value fine formula in Sec. 3(e)) and are recorded under enforcement, not here. The AI-assistance aggravator is a binary condition, not a numeric threshold, and the bill sets no value-based penalty tier.
